tasks.title: Narrow the NotificationItem Text-node promise to what holds for an empty message, and pin the empty case
acceptance:
C1 (preserved, newly tested; passes at 292bee6 by design). `src/renderer/src/notifications/NotificationProvider.test.tsx` gains a test that, for each of the three kinds `error`, `info` and `success`, calls `notify({ kind, message: '' })` inside a provider and finds exactly one item of that `data-kind` whose message element (the item's `role="alert"` or `role="status"` element) has `childNodes.length === 0` and `textContent === ''`. What it preserves: an empty message is rendered as given, not rejected, rewritten or dropped. The behaviour was measured at 292bee6 with the worktree's react 19.2.8 and jsdom: a `

` whose only child is `''` has 0 child nodes and `textContent` `""`, and one whose child is `'x'` has 1.

C2. The C1 test is shown able to fail by demonstrated discrimination. At the single site `{message}` inside the message `

` of `src/renderer/src/notifications/NotificationItem.tsx` (line 54 at 292bee6; `{message}` occurs once in the file), inject `{message === '' ? ' ' : message}`. This is type-valid and changes only empty-message rendering. Then run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/notifications/NotificationProvider.test.tsx`, observe the C1 test fail while the existing first-Text-node test (the one titled '... first Text node (C8)'; that `(C8)` is an earlier session's label, not this manifest's C8) still passes, revert, and confirm the revert by reading the line back before running anything wider. The report names the site, the command, the failure output and the revert.

C3. The leading docblock of `src/renderer/src/notifications/NotificationItem.tsx` no longer says that the message element's first child is a Text node for every message. It says the element holds nothing but `message` (no longer 'as its only child', which is false for an empty message), and it still says the dismiss control is a sibling, never inside it. It states both cases: for a non-empty message, the first child is the one Text node React renders, and for an empty message, the element has no child nodes and its `textContent` is `''`. At 292bee6 the docblock (lines 9-11) states the non-empty case only.

C4. The docblock states the rule in place. It cites no session id, no `.sir/sessions` path and no file under `contracts/` that resolves only under `.sir/`. Check: `git grep -c --untracked 2026111 -- src/renderer/src/notifications/NotificationItem.tsx src/renderer/src/notifications/NotificationProvider.test.tsx` prints nothing and exits 1, as it does at 292bee6.

C5. No existing test in `NotificationProvider.test.tsx` is weakened. `git diff -U0 -- src/renderer/src/notifications/NotificationProvider.test.tsx` shows no removed line, that is, no line beginning with a single `-` other than the `---` header. The existing first-Text-node test ('gives the message element the kind’s live role and the message as its first Text node (C8)') keeps every assertion it has at 292bee6.

C6. The new test's name states the condition (an empty message) and the outcome (an empty message element with no child nodes). It does not say 'works' or claim more than it asserts. This encodes the binding test discipline rule under `Naming`: 'A test name states the condition and the expected outcome'.
C7. `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/notifications` exits 0 with the injection reverted. The report quotes vitest's `Test Files` and `Tests` summary lines.

tasks.title: Give the focused empty notification viewport a visible minimum size, and update the N7 step 5 prediction
acceptance: C8. In `src/renderer/src/notifications/Notifications.module.css`, the rule whose selector is `.viewport:focus-visible` declares `min-width` and `min-height`. Each value is a single `var(--oc-space-N)`, and N is 4, 6 or 8: those tokens are 16px, 24px and 32px at `src/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:139-141`, so the focused empty box is at least 16px in each axis. The space tokens below them are 4px, 8px and 12px (`tokens.css:136-138`), and the bare outline is the 'small blue square about 4 px across' that N7 step 5 predicts. At 292bee6 that rule (lines 20-22) holds only `outline`, so this criterion fails there.

C9. `src/renderer/src/notifications/Notifications.styles.test.ts` gains a declaration-level test that, through the file's own `ruleFor('.viewport:focus-visible')`, asserts the C8 `min-width` and `min-height` declarations and that each names a space token of 16px or more. Red step: write the test first, run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/notifications/Notifications.styles.test.ts` against the unmodified stylesheet, and report the failing assertion. Only then edit the CSS.

C10 (preserved). The `.viewport:focus-visible` rule still declares `outline: var(--oc-border-thick) solid var(--oc-focus-ring)`. The stylesheet still contains no `outline: none`, no `outline: 0` and no `!important`. The existing 'focus rings' and 'never fights the cascade and never removes the focus ring' tests in `Notifications.styles.test.ts` pass with their assertions unchanged, and `git diff -U0` of that file shows no removed line beginning with a single `-`.

C11 (preserved, newly tested). The unfocused `.viewport` rule's size is unchanged. Its body declares no `min-width`, `min-height`, `height`, `padding` or `padding-*`, and it keeps `width: max-content` and `max-width: calc(var(--oc-lane-rail-width) * 2)`, as at 292bee6 (lines 8-18). This keeps the region from becoming a fixed box in the corner that intercepts clicks when it is not focused. A new test asserts it through `ruleFor('.viewport')`. That test is shown able to fail: inject `min-height: var(--oc-space-6);` into the `.viewport` rule body only, run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/notifications/Notifications.styles.test.ts`, observe the new test fail, revert, and confirm the revert. The report names the site, the command and the output.
C12. The new tests' names state the condition and the outcome. This encodes the binding test discipline rule under `Naming`.

C13. `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/notifications/Notifications.styles.test.ts` exits 0 with every injection reverted. This includes the existing token test, which allows only names in `TOKENS`, and the hardcoded-colour test. The report quotes the `Tests` summary line.

C14. In `docs/human-checks/message-alerting.md`, N7 step 5 no longer says the empty region 'has no padding' or that its outline 'should be only a small blue square about 4 px across'. It predicts the outline from the C8 minimum size, naming the token and its px value and citing the CSS line that declares it. It still says the size was not measured. N7 stays open: nothing in the file or in this task records the check as made, and N7's 'Passes when' paragraph is unchanged.

C15. Every citation in `docs/human-checks/message-alerting.md` of the form `Notifications.module.css:<line or range>` names, at T3's tip, the line or lines carrying what its sentence describes. Lines move when declarations are added under `.viewport:focus-visible`, and the `.dismiss:focus-visible` citation (`:63-65` at 292bee6) and the `.message` citation (`:46`) sit below that rule. At 292bee6, `grep -o 'Notifications.module.css:[0-9-]*' docs/human-checks/message-alerting.md` prints 7 citations. The report lists each one with its old and new value.

C16. No session-id citation is added to `src`. `git grep -c --untracked 2026111 -- src/renderer/src/notifications/Notifications.module.css src/renderer/src/notifications/Notifications.styles.test.ts` prints nothing and exits 1, as at 292bee6. Each added CSS comment or test docblock states its rule in place.

tasks.title: Raise an untitled info `Pod stopped` when a stop succeeds for an unlisted Pod, with the missing row test; repo-wide gates
acceptance: C17. A new jsdom test file, `src/renderer/src/pods/PodsChrome.test.tsx`, reaches `PodsChrome`'s stop handler with a Pod id that `pods.value` does not hold. It renders the real `PodsChrome` inside the real `NotificationProvider` and the real `WorkspaceProvider`, driven by `stubOrcastrateApi` with at least one listed Pod. The ONLY module it mocks is `./PodBarPanel`, through `vi.mock`, to capture the props `PodsChrome` passes, on the precedent of `src/renderer/src/shell/App.panelSlots.test.tsx:22`. Its docblock says why the panel is mocked: no rendered control reaches an unlisted stop. `PodBarPanel` renders only rows of `tabs` (its optimistic order resolves through the current `tabs` and falls back to them), `PodBar` renders one `PodTab` per row, `PodsChrome` passes `tabs={pods.value}` and `onClose={handleStop}` from the same render, and `handleStop` reads the title from that same `pods.value`. The docblock names this code by symbol (`PodBarPanel`, `PodBar`, `onClose={handleStop}`, `tabs={pods.value}`, `handleStop`) and cites no line number, because this task edits `PodsChrome.tsx` and the lines move. (At 292bee6 the sites are `PodBarPanel.tsx:64-73`, `PodBar.tsx:94-102` and `PodsChrome.tsx:157`, `:342`, `:350`, for the implementer's orientation only.) This encodes the binding test discipline rule 'A mock stands in for a boundary the test cannot cross'. If the implementer finds a rendered route after all, the test drives that route instead of the mock, and the report names it as file:line.

C18. In that file, a test calls the captured `onClose` with an unlisted Pod id. The stub's `pods.close` resolves ok. Afterwards the notification viewport holds exactly one item with `data-kind` `info`, and the `textContent` of its `role="status"` message element is exactly `Pod stopped`. Red step: write this test first, run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/pods/PodsChrome.test.tsx` against `PodsChrome.tsx` as at 292bee6, where `if (title === undefined) return;` (line 164) raises nothing, and report the failure output. Only then implement.

C19 (preserved, newly tested). In the C18 test, the stub records exactly one `podClose` call, and its argument is the unlisted id (`api.calls.podClose` equals `[[<that id>]]`). What it preserves: `closePod` is called for an unlisted Pod, as at 292bee6 (`PodsChrome.tsx:158`). This matches the recommended option, not the alternative of matching `handleRun`/`handleRequestDelete` and skipping the call.

C20. The untitled notification carries key `pod-close`. A test makes two successive successful unlisted stops through the captured `onClose`, waiting for each to settle, and finds exactly one `info` item reading `Pod stopped`. An unkeyed notify would leave two, because `handleStop`'s leading `notifier.dismiss('pod-close')` removes only keyed items. At 292bee6 the viewport holds zero items, so this test fails there.

C21 (preserved, newly tested). Through the same captured `onClose`, a stop of the LISTED Pod raises exactly one `info` item reading `Pod stopped: <that Pod's title>`. This shows the seam drives the real handler. It is shown able to fail: inject a change to the listed-case template literal inside `handleStop` only (for example, drop the space after the colon), run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/pods/PodsChrome.test.tsx`, observe the failure, revert, and confirm the revert. The report names the file:line.

C22 (preserved, newly tested). With `api.failInvoke('podClose', ipcError(<code>, <a message unique to this test>))`, an unlisted stop raises exactly one `error` item. The `textContent` of its `role="alert"` message element equals that message verbatim, and no item reads `Pod stopped`. It is shown able to fail by injecting at the error-branch `message: result.error.message` inside `handleStop` only (line 160 at 292bee6; the same text also occurs in `handleFork`, `handleReorder` and `handleRun`, which are not to be touched), for example by appending a character in a template literal. Run the same scoped command, observe the failure, revert and confirm.

C23. The comments in `handleStop` describe what the code now does. The docblock above `handleStop` and the comment at the unlisted branch say that a successful stop of a Pod `pods.value` does not hold raises the untitled info `Pod stopped` with key `pod-close`. No comment in `PodsChrome.tsx` still says an unlisted stop raises nothing; at 292bee6 the comment at line 163 implies that. No comment claims the branch is reachable from the rendered Pod bar.

C24. The unlisted case is handled explicitly as a legitimate state. The title lookup is narrowed with a check, with no non-null assertion (`!`) and no `as` cast, and it does not throw. This encodes the binding frontend fragment rule under 'Indexed access under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`': 'Where absence is a legitimate state rather than a defect, handle it explicitly … instead of throwing', and 'Do not use a non-null assertion (`!`) … Do not use a type cast (`as`)'.
C25. Every new test's name states the condition and the outcome. This encodes the binding test discipline rule under `Naming`.

C26 (preserved). `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/__tests__/message-alerting.e2e.test.tsx src/renderer/src/__tests__/pod-stop.e2e.test.tsx src/renderer/src/pods` exits 0. This includes the S6 test 'S6 raises an info notification naming the Pod when closePod resolves ok' (`Pod stopped: Alpha`), which is unchanged.

C27. No session-id or `.sir/sessions` citation is added to `src` anywhere in the session. This is the repo-wide census, run at T2's tip after T1 and T3 have landed. (a) `git grep -l --untracked 2026111 -- src | wc -l` prints 8, as at 292bee6. (b) `git grep -c --untracked 2026111 -- src/renderer/src/pods/PodsChrome.tsx src/renderer/src/pods/PodsChrome.test.tsx` prints exactly `src/renderer/src/pods/PodsChrome.tsx:1`: the base value for that file is 1, at line 37, and the new file has 0. (c) `git grep -l --untracked .sir/sessions -- src | wc -l` prints 1, as at 292bee6, where the one file is `src/renderer/src/notifications/types.ts`, which no task touches.

C28. `npm run typecheck` exits 0 at T2's tip. This is repo-wide: `typecheck:node` and `typecheck:web`. Vitest does not typecheck, so this is the only check that covers T1's, T2's and T3's test files under `tsc`.
C29. `npm test` (unscoped `vitest run`) exits 0 at T2's tip, with no injection live anywhere. The report quotes vitest's `Test Files` and `Tests` summary lines as printed.
